text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where code changes are automatically built and tested frequently. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, developers merge their work into a shared repository several times a day. Here, CI pipelines take over: they automatically compile the code, run a full suite of tests, and check for errors. This process is crucial for catching issues early. When a problem occurs, developers are alerted immediately, making it much cheaper and faster to fix. As a result, teams produce more stable software, avoid painful last-minute surprises, and maintain a steady, confident pace of development.
